_readme: Golden sample for Cisco SERVER / HyperFlex parts, extracted from PDF spec sheets.
WHY A SECOND FILE. cisco-switches.golden.json covers ten Catalyst PIDs. Run against the PDF
corpus the gate reported precision 0.0% and FAIL, which reads as catastrophically bad data
and was nothing of the sort -- the two sets simply do not intersect. The gate now reports
UNVERIFIED for that case, and this file is what turns UNVERIFIED into a real verdict for
server data.
HOW THESE WERE VERIFIED. Read directly out of the cached PDF with pdfplumber, page 22 of
hci-220m7-specsheet.pdf, and transcribed by hand from the printed table:
Product ID       | Segment/Workload   | Max Socket | Cores | Clock Freq | Power | Cache Size | Highest DDR5
HCI-CPU-I8558U1  | 1-Socket Optimized | 1S         | 48    | 2.00       | 300   | 260.00     | 4800
NOT copied from the extractor's own output, which would be a tautology that passes however
wrong the pipeline is.
THE ARITHMETIC AND THE TRAPS, checked by hand:
- This table's units live in the SECOND header row, so the extractor sees 'Cores' and the
bare value '60'. cpu_cores has canonical unit 'cores', which is a counting word and not
a convertible unit, so a bare number is the correct and only form.
- 'Power (W)' here is on a CPU option PID, so it is that PROCESSOR's TDP -- not the
chassis draw. It must land on tdp and never on power_max, or a server's power budget
would be silently replaced by one component's.
- 'Maximum Socket = 1S' is a count; the trailing S is the word socket, not a unit.
- 'Highest DDR5 DIMM Clock' is printed under MT/s here and under MHz on the DDR4 sheets.
The figures are DDR transfer rates in both cases, so the canonical unit is MT/s.
- 'Cache Size 300.00' is megabytes per the header; the trailing .00 is formatting.
